title: Generative Modeling by Value-Driven Transport
claim: Continuous-time transport follows smooth curved ODE paths, while discrete-time transport maps states through a sequence of policy steps.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, left-to-right, shapes morph along trajectories with dots marking steps
description: Two side-by-side panels show the same transport from a blob-like orange distribution on the left to a pink star-shaped distribution on the right. Intermediate shapes sit between them and change gradually from orange to pink. In the left panel, three black curved arrows start at points in the source and end at points in the target. They run inside a pale yellow tube, which suggests continuous smooth ODE paths. In the right panel, the same three trajectories are drawn as piecewise-linear segments. Black dots mark the discrete states at each intermediate shape, and arrows join them step by step to show a sequence of policies. There are no text labels. The eye goes first to the bright orange-to-magenta shapes, then to the contrast between the curved and the stepwise paths.
caption: Continuous- and discrete-time transport plans. Continuous-time plans are defined as smooth solutions of ODEs parametrized by a continuous-time control drift, whereas discrete-time plans are defined by a sequence of control policies directly mapping states to next states.
abstract: We propose a new framework for generative modeling based on a discrete-time stochastic control formulation of measure transport. Adapting classic results from control theory, we formulate our problem as a linear program whose dual variables correspond to the \emph{optimal value function} of the control problem, which directly encodes the optimal control policy. Exploiting this LP formulation, we develop an efficient simulation-free primal-dual algorithm for computing approximately optimal value functions and the associated \emph{value-driven transport} (VDT) policies which approximate the true optimal policy. We show that well-trained VDT policies enjoy numerous favorable properties in comparison with other state-of-the-art methods based on flows, diffusions, or SchrÃ¶dinger bridges: they lead to straight transport paths which can be simulated quickly and robustly, and can be enhanced in all the same ways as diffusion and flow-based models (e.g., conditional generation, classifier-free guidance, unpaired data-to-data translation are all easy to incorporate). We evaluate our methodology in a range of experiments, with results that indicate strong performance and good potential for scalability.
